# Linting the whole tree under full enforcement

The repository carries the lint binary and the configuration every contributor's
change is held to. One command answers whether the tree is clean right now.

## Run it

```bash
.ok-plumbline/bin/plumbline .
```

Over the repository root, under the shipped configuration, the lint exits 0 with
no output.

The configuration at `.ok-plumbline/config.json` switches off no check, and
declares five citation tags: `@concept:`, `@story:`, `@decision:`, `@subject:`,
`@practice:`. The verdict is under full enforcement, not a reduced set.

The lint is a node script, so `node` must be on PATH.

## Prove the checks are live

A clean run proves nothing if the checks are inert. Put a throwaway tree
carrying one seeded file in front of the same binary under a copy of the same
configuration.

A stray comment:

```go
package main

// a prose comment nobody asked for
func main() {}
```

```bash
.ok-plumbline/bin/plumbline .
# exit 2, reporting plumbline/comment-hygiene
```

A citation that resolves to nothing:

```go
package main

// @concept: no-such-concept
func main() {}
```

```bash
.ok-plumbline/bin/plumbline .
# exit 2, reporting plumbline/citation-unresolved
```

A citation that does resolve:

```go
package main

// @concept: node
func main() {}
```

```bash
.ok-plumbline/bin/plumbline .
# exit 0
```

The citation check discriminates rather than always failing, and the comment
check fires rather than sitting inert. A green verdict over the repository is a
statement about the tree.
